card.name: Matching term in a comparison phrase
card.fires_on: The second, repeated or paired word in a matched comparison, such as 'gram for gram', 'mg-to-mg', '12 noon ... 12 noon' or 'incidence in drug ... incidence in placebo'. Also fires on some words after 'bilateral' or 'corresponding'.

modes.label: Dose-for-dose equivalence
modes.description: The repeated unit in a one-to-one dose conversion phrase.
modes.example: initiate treatment at the same dose (gram for<< gram>>) and regimen as Xyrem.

modes.label: Split paired term
modes.description: The end of a repeated or split word completing a paired comparison, such as mg-to-mg, BID or incidence.
modes.example: OMCAZIO is not substitutable on a mg-to-m<<g>> basis with other cabozantinib

modes.label: General matched pair
modes.description: A word that closes a parallel or comparative pair in ordinary prose.
modes.example: the species would not be all the same in the apparently corresponding<< stages>> in the two regions.

card.plain: It lights up on the second half of a matched pair, like 'gram for gram' or 'mg to mg'.
